title: The Grove Learning Circuit Logic

features.name: the-bark-that-learned-to-trace
features.desc-on-touch: wood grain becomes circuit—the tree has read something in the ground beneath it and is writing the answer in its own rings; each year adds a line to the diagram

features.name: the-root-wire-convergence
features.desc-on-touch: roots spread here like traces on a board, each following a logic older than electricity—but now they seem to be reading each other, learning the language the circuit boards learned from imitating them

features.name: the-signal-that-the-grove-sends
features.desc-on-touch: between the trees, a pattern of light and static—the archive believes the grove is broadcasting something back to the forest, not speech, but a kind of conversation in the language of sap and signal

features.name: the-branch-that-remembers-board-logic
features.desc-on-touch: a single branch has grown into the shape of a circuit path, or perhaps the path was always there and the branch learned to read it; either way, the grove is teaching itself to think like the archive

features.name: the-canopy-that-broadcasts
features.desc-on-touch: above, the leaves settle into patterns—not random, not organized, but choosing themselves into a configuration that speaks to something listening from far away; the grove has learned to signal

inscription: the forest and its double read each other in a language neither was taught; the grove broadcasts back to everything it learns

file.name: Grove_Signal_Patterns_Static_Traces.mp3
file.note: recording of the grove's broadcast—circuit-sounds emerging from bark, the archive realizing that forest root-logic and board-logic speak the same language, only written in different scales
